title: Low magnon damping of a EuSe film down to millikelvin temperatures
authors: Rostyslav O. Serha, Jan Hofer, Khrystyna O. Levchenko, Andreas Ney, Sergej O. Demokritov, Gunther Springholz, Andrii V. Chumak
abstract: The rapid development of quantum magnonics over the past decade has created a demand for magnetic materials that keep their magnon losses low at millikelvin temperatures and add functionality beyond that of the established iron garnets and ferromagnetic metals. The europium chalcogenides are natural candidates $-$ they are magnetic semiconductors whose moment of $7\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}$ per Eu$^{2+}$ ion stems from a half-filled $4f$ shell with zero orbital momentum, so that spin-orbit coupling and intrinsic damping are expected to be weak. Here we characterize an epitaxial film of the metamagnet EuSe on diamagnetic BaF$_2$ by magnetometry and broadband ferromagnetic resonance from 10 K down to 30 mK. EuSe combines a saturation magnetization of 1100 kA/m with antiferromagnetic, ferrimagnetic and ferromagnetic phases that are reached with fields below 0.25 T. In contrast to a Gilbert-damped ferromagnet, the linewidth of the field-aligned film decreases with increasing frequency and field, and below 750 mK it no longer depends on temperature. At 30 mK, 68 GHz and 1.8 T, it reaches 5.5 mT, close to the values of bulk single crystals, which corresponds to a magnon lifetime of 2 ns and to an upper bound of $1.1\times10^{-3}$ for the Gilbert damping parameter. These properties make EuSe and the europium chalcogenides promising materials for hybrid quantum systems and quantum magnonics.
summary: This work characterizes the magnetic properties of EuSe thin films, focusing on magnon damping down to millikelvin temperatures. Using broadband FMR, the authors demonstrate that EuSe exhibits remarkably low magnon losses, suggesting its potential as a superior material for next-generation quantum magnonics and hybrid quantum devices.
main_problem: The central goal is to find magnetic materials with extremely low magnon damping at millikelvin temperatures for use in quantum magnonics.
main_result: EuSe films exhibit significantly low magnon damping ($\alpha_{eff} \le 1.1 	imes 10^{-3}$) at 30 mK, which is highly promising for hybrid quantum systems.
method: The study uses broadband Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) measurements, complemented by magnetometry, across temperatures from 10 K down to 30 mK.
model_or_system: The physical system is an epitaxial film of the metamagnet EuSe grown on a diamagnetic BaF2 substrate. The material is characterized by its magnetic phases (AFM, FiM, FM) and its intrinsic magnetic excitations (magnons).
key_observables: FMR linewidth ($\Delta B$), magnon lifetime ($	au$), saturation magnetization ($M_{sat}$), and the Gilbert damping parameter ($\alpha$).
important_parameters: Temperatures down to 30 mK, frequencies up to 68 GHz, and a low upper bound for the damping parameter ($1.1 	imes 10^{-3}$).
main_assumptions: The intrinsic linewidth calculation requires correction factors, and the analysis assumes the system behaves like an in-plane magnetized film for Kittel fits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the H-T phase diagram, static magnetization sweeps showing metamagnetic transitions, and FMR transmission dips used to extract the intrinsic linewidth as a function of frequency and temperature.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for low-loss magnetic materials. It then details the experimental characterization using FMR and magnetometry across a wide temperature range, presenting results showing the temperature-independent, low-damping behavior of EuSe at cryogenic temperatures.
why_interesting: The extremely low, temperature-independent magnon damping observed at millikelvin temperatures provides a platform for studying coherent quantum dynamics in solid-state magnetic systems, relevant to quantum information storage and processing.
